title: Pro Defensione Trium Capitulorum Concilii Chalcedoniensis Libri XII
author: Facundus of Hermiane
source: Translated by Claude from tmp1122.tmp1122.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina.
statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

passages.original: Ac ne hoc dis- simulent intelligere, aut fortasse uon possint, verborum suorum vel convincantur vel admoneantur exemplo. Nam et ipsi, cum recte dicant unam ex Trinitate personam crucifixam, secundum quod ille etiam vir beatus et doctrinae admirabilis Augustinus, in opere quod scripsit de Prædestinatione et persevcrantia sanctorum, docet 5 : < Fidelis qui in eo veram naturam credit et contitetur humanam, id est nostram, quamvis singulariter suscipientc Deo Verbo, in unicum Dei Filium sublimatam : ita ut qui suscepit, et quod suscepit, una esset in Trinitate persona. > Cum igitur et ipsi, quemadmodum docuimus I, juxta docLriuam Patrum recte dicant unam ex Trinitate personam crucifixam ;
passages.english: And so that they may not pretend not to understand this, or perhaps be unable to, let them be either refuted or admonished by the example of their own words. For they too rightly say that one person of the Trinity was crucified, according to what that blessed man of admirable teaching, Augustine, also teaches in the work he wrote On the Predestination and Perseverance of the Saints: "He is faithful who believes and confesses in him a true human nature, that is, ours, though raised up in a singular way, God the Word taking it up, into the only Son of God, so that he who took up and what he took up were one person in the Trinity." Since, therefore, they too, as we have shown, rightly say according to the teaching of the Fathers that one person of the Trinity was crucified;
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected (e.g. 'uon' for 'non', 'contitetur' for 'confitetur', 'docLriuam' for 'doctrinam'); stray marks '5' and 'I' omitted. The sentence continues in the following passage.

passages.original: Nam et ille centurio, qui corpus Domini gloriæ crucifixi servabat, cum eispirante mundi' Creatore, mundi videret elementa turbari, Filiutn Dei eum verum I esse cognovit; ait enim : Vere Filius Dei erat iste (Matth. XXVII, 54). Cujus verbi fidem beatus facit Hilarius, ita dicens (Lib. III de Trmitate): « Qui cruci affixerant, vere Dei Filium confilentur ; praedicationi consentit eSectus. Dominus dixerat : Clarifica Filium tuum (Joan. XVII, 1). Non solum nomine contestatus est Filium, sed et proprietate qua dicitur tuum. Multi enim nos filii Dei, sed non talis hic Filius est. Hic enim et proprius et verus est Filius, origine non adoptione, veritate non nuncupatione, nativitale non creatione.
passages.english: For that centurion too, who was guarding the body of the crucified Lord of glory, when he saw the elements of the world thrown into turmoil as the Creator of the world breathed his last, recognized that he was the true Son of God; for he says: "Truly this was the Son of God" (Matt. 27:54). The blessed Hilary confirms the faith of this saying, speaking thus (On the Trinity, book 3): "Those who had fastened him to the cross confess that he is truly the Son of God; the outcome agrees with the proclamation. The Lord had said: 'Glorify your Son' (John 17:1). He attested [him as] Son not only by name but also by the property by which he says 'your'. For we are many sons of God, but this Son is not such. For this one is both the proper and the true Son, by origin not adoption, in truth not by naming, by birth not by creation.

passages.original: Cum vero hoc adjecit dicens, I ne non Trinitas, sed quaternitas crederetur, » coegit omnino ut beatam Alanam veraciter et proprie matrem Dei esse dicamus, ne non Trinitatem, sed quaternitatem credere videamur. Et ideo religiosæ ac necessariæ vocis hujus negatio non levis putetur, quam tanta blasphemia consequitur. Sane intrandum non est quod Augustinus veraciter et proprie dici pronuntiat filium hominis Deum, cum in quodam sermone de Epiphania (De tempore aerm. 33), cujus principium est: I Nuper celebravimus diem quo ex Judæis Dominus natus est, hodie celebramus quo a gentibus adoratus est, » ita loquatur : < Magos sane ad ipsum proprie locum, ubi Deus Verbum infans erat, stella perduxit. » Quod 1 ergo a Verbum Deum dicit infantem, quomodo non veraciter et proprie diceret prædicari filium hominis Deum ?
passages.english: But when he added this, saying, "lest not a Trinity but a quaternity be believed," he compelled us absolutely to say that blessed Mary is truly and properly the mother of God, lest we seem to believe not in a Trinity but in a quaternity. And therefore let the denial of this pious and necessary expression, which is followed by so great a blasphemy, not be thought a light matter. Certainly one should not wonder that Augustine declares that God is truly and properly called son of man, since in a certain sermon on the Epiphany (De tempore, sermon 33), whose opening is: "Recently we celebrated the day on which the Lord was born of the Jews; today we celebrate the day on which he was worshipped by the gentiles," he speaks thus: "The star led the Magi properly to the very place where God the Word was an infant." Since, then, he calls God the Word an infant, how would he not say that God is truly and properly proclaimed son of man?
passages.notes: 'Alanam' read as 'Mariam'; 'intrandum' read as 'mirandum'; 'aerm.' as 'serm.'. Stray '1' and 'a' omitted.

passages.original: Quia igitur utraque pars Eutychianorum ipsius synodi auctoritatem sequi se dicit, sufficere confutationi eorum existimo, si aliis omissis hoc solum clareat, quod ipsa quoque duas firmaverit Christi esse naturas, cum protulit adversus Nestorium ex secundo libro beati Ambrosii ad Gratianum imperatorem (Cap. 4), dicens 6 : « Sileant igitur inanes de sermonibus quæmones: quia regnum Dci, sicut scriptum est, non in persuasione verbi est, sed in ostensione virtutis. Ser- vemus distinctionem divinitatis et carnis : unus in utraque loquitur Dei Filius, quia in eodem utraque natura est. Et si idem loquitur, non uno semper loquiturmodo. » Intende in eo nunc gloriam Dei, nunchomi- nis passiones.
passages.english: Since, therefore, both parties of the Eutychians say that they follow the authority of that synod, I think it suffices for their refutation if, leaving other things aside, this alone is made clear: that it too affirmed that there are two natures of Christ, when against Nestorius it brought forward [a passage] from the second book of blessed Ambrose to the emperor Gratian (ch. 4), saying: "Let empty questions about words therefore fall silent, for the kingdom of God, as it is written, is not in the persuasiveness of speech but in the display of power. Let us keep the distinction of the divinity and the flesh: the one Son of God speaks in both, because both natures are in the same [one]. And if the same one speaks, he does not always speak in one manner." Observe in him now the glory of God, now the sufferings of man.
passages.notes: 'quæmones' read as 'quaestiones'. The last sentence is probably still part of the Ambrose quotation, though the edition closes the quotation marks before it.

passages.original: > Isti vero e contrario camdem Tbeodorum in Evangelii expositione reprehendunt, in quo labores ejus, quisquis est auctor illius operis, I perhibet quod nullus ausus fuerit increpare, sed dextro potius honorare decreto: et hinc cum impium vocant, quod Dominum in passione, et formidasse b, et turbatum esse dixerit, ita ut hoc quoque dicerent: < Horremus etiam solum memoriam blasphemiarum ejus, et Deo supplicamus ut nobis fiat propitius, quod omnino in lingua talia sustinemus asserentes trepidare in passione eum posse, qui suis famulis qui pro ejus nomine martyrium susceperunt talem donavit gratiam, ut cum gaudio et promptitudine et alacritate passiones adirent.» Haec autem reprebensio et detestatio scriptorum Theodori sanam doctrinam beati Leonis synodi Chalcedonensis auctoris impu- gnat 1, qui scribens Juvenali Hierosolymitano epi scopo dicit (Epist. 78) : < Utere igilur, frater charissirne, invictissimis catiholicæ fidei documentis. ct evangelistarum prædicationem sanctorum locorum in quibus degis tcstificatione dcfende.
passages.english: But these men, on the contrary, censure the same Theodore in an exposition of the Gospel, though in it (whoever is the author of that work) it is stated of his labours that no one dared rebuke them, but rather to honour [them] with a favourable verdict; and from this they call him impious because he said that the Lord in his passion both feared and was troubled, so that they even said this: "We shudder even at the mere memory of his blasphemies, and we pray God to be merciful to us because we endure at all in our tongue such men, who assert that he could tremble in his passion who gave such grace to his servants who underwent martyrdom for his name that they went to their sufferings with joy, readiness and eagerness." But this censure and detestation of Theodore's writings attacks the sound teaching of blessed Leo, the author of the synod of Chalcedon, who writing to Juvenal, bishop of Jerusalem, says (Letter 78): "Use, therefore, dearest brother, the most invincible proofs of the catholic faith, and defend the preaching of the evangelists by the testimony of the holy places in which you dwell.
passages.notes: The syntax of the first sentence is awkward in the Latin ('in quo... perhibet'); rendered by sense. 'in lingua talia sustinemus' is obscure; 'talia' may refer to such assertions or such people.

passages.original: Quid porro est, quod in codem libro in quo Theodorus dicitur diaboli transgressus insaniam, quia Dominum nostrum in passione formidasse et turbatum esse confessus est, Atbanasius approbatur, quod in libro tertio adversus Arianos c scribens de proprietatibus duarum Christi naturarum, hoc etiam dicat:« Etenim perturbari carnis proprium est: potestatem autem habere ponendi et sumendi quando vult animam, non est hoc proprium hominis, sed Verbi virtutis est? » Ecce ipsi non alibi, sed in eodem libro, immemores sui, fatentur quod beatus Athanasius veraciter in passione Dominum dixerit esse turbatum. Cur ergo sibi contrarii, in quo Athanastum probant, ut magno concilio præjudicent, Theodorum damnant ?Qui beatus Athanasius iia locutus esi etiam in lihro quem de Trinitate conscripsit: « Verbum enim et Filius Dei semper erat Dominus Dens, et non post crucifixionem factus est Dominus Jesus Christus, sed, ut prædixi, humanitatem ejus effecit divinitas Dominum et Deum.
passages.english: What, moreover, of the fact that in the same book in which Theodore is said to have surpassed the madness of the devil because he confessed that our Lord in his passion feared and was troubled, Athanasius is approved, who in the third book against the Arians, writing on the properties of the two natures of Christ, says this too: "For to be troubled is proper to the flesh; but to have power to lay down and take up the soul when he wills is not proper to man, but belongs to the power of the Word"? See, they themselves, not elsewhere but in the same book, forgetful of themselves, admit that blessed Athanasius truly said the Lord was troubled in his passion. Why then, contradicting themselves, do they condemn Theodore in that for which they approve Athanasius, so as to prejudice the great council? This blessed Athanasius also spoke thus in the book he wrote on the Trinity: "For the Word and Son of God was always Lord God, and he was not made Lord Jesus Christ after the crucifixion; but, as I said before, the divinity made his humanity Lord and God.

passages.original: neque jam probemus quod ista res hæreticum non faciat, cum saepe laudabile jutlicetur, si etiam moraliter exponantur quæ prophetice dicta sunt : his terminum contentionibus dant quae a idem Theodorus in libro de allegoria et historia quem contra Origenem scripsit (undc ct odium Origenianorum incurrit) dicit ad Cerdonem : 4 Ego quidem , quod nostra sic laudes, non alii cuipiam imputo, quam amicitiæ quam circa nos habes, quam etiam in multis et magnis rebus semper osten - disti;
passages.english: and let us not now prove that this matter does not make [one] a heretic, since it is often judged praiseworthy if things spoken prophetically are also expounded morally: those words put an end to these disputes which the same Theodore, in the book on allegory and history that he wrote against Origen (from which he also incurred the hatred of the Origenists), says to Cerdo: "For my part, that you praise my works thus, I attribute to nothing else than the friendship you have towards us, which you have also always shown in many great matters;
passages.notes: Begins mid-sentence; 'jutlicetur' read as 'judicetur'. 'Cerdo' unidentified addressee.

passages.original: Sed isti, qui hæresi deputant, si quædam prophetice in Christum dicta cliam moraliter exponantur, cogitare debent quomodo beatum Cyrillum possint defondere. In illo enim opere, quod eum scripsisse dicunt in reprehensionem quorumdam dictorum Diodori atque Theodori, tate aliquid invenitur, ut si adhuc ab ipso compositum dicarIt, hæreticum eum fuisse confirment. Namque auctor ejusdem operis trartat ibi capitulum, in quo ad Hebræos dicit Apostolus : Non enim angelis subjecit orbem terræ futu um, de quo loquimur. Testatus est autem in quodam loco quis dicens (Hebr. II, a, 9) : Quid es! homo, quod memor es ejus, aut filius hominis, quoniam visitas eum ? Minuisti eum paulo minus ab angelis, gloria et honore coronasti eum, et constituisti eum super opera manuum tuarum : omnia subjecisti sub pedibus ejus (Psal.
passages.english: But these men, who count it as heresy if certain things spoken prophetically of Christ are also expounded morally, ought to consider how they can defend blessed Cyril. For in that work which they say he wrote in censure of certain sayings of Diodore and Theodore, something of this kind is found, so that if they still say it was composed by him, they would confirm that he was a heretic. For the author of that work treats there the chapter in which the Apostle says to the Hebrews: "For he did not subject to angels the world to come, of which we speak. But someone has testified somewhere, saying (Heb. 2:5-9): 'What is man, that you are mindful of him, or the son of man, that you visit him? You made him a little lower than the angels, you crowned him with glory and honour, and set him over the works of your hands; you subjected all things under his feet' (Ps.
passages.notes: 'tate' read as 'tale'; 'dicarIt' as 'dicant'; 'futu um' as 'futurum'. Passage ends mid-citation (Ps. 8).

passages.original: Quid etiam quod, sicut jam memoravimus, ila di- cunt ab eodem Cyrillo reprehensum esse Theodorum, ut sanctum quoque Diodorum, magistrum ipsius Theodori, pariter ab eo et in eadem causa dicant fuisse culpatum Si igitur auctoritatem Cyrilli secuti sunt, Theodorum damnantes1, quanquam dicere non audeant quod ille Theodoro anathema dixerit, cujus etiam scripta anathematizare prohibuit, quare tamen, non Diodorum quoque damnaverunt?
passages.english: What too of the fact that, as we have already mentioned, they say Theodore was censured by the same Cyril in such a way that they say holy Diodore too, the teacher of Theodore himself, was likewise blamed by him and in the same cause? If therefore they followed Cyril's authority in condemning Theodore, although they do not dare to say that he pronounced anathema on Theodore, whose writings he even forbade to be anathematized, why then did they not condemn Diodore as well?

passages.original: Incipiamus itaque jam predictorum venerabilium Patrum testimonia recensere, quibus commendatur Diodorus, quem cum Theodoro pariter et in eadem causa culpatum dicunt a Cyrillo, velut ea docentem quæ Nestorius docuit: ut quia sine magistro suo cum quo illi causa communis est, non potuit juste Theodorus condemnari , cum probaverimus Diodorum non esse damnandum , multo amplius manifestum fiat omnibus pro solo præjudicio synodi Chalcedonensis, inique Theodorum fuissc damnatum. Beatus igitur Athanasius ita memorato sancto Diodoro scribit : < Domino meo filio et amantissimo consacerdoti, episcopo Tarsi Diodoro, Athanasius in Domino salutem. Gratias Domino meo, qui ubicunque suam doctrinam fundat, et maxime per filios proprios, qualem et te ipsum res ipsa demonstrat.
passages.english: Let us therefore now begin to review the testimonies of the aforesaid venerable Fathers by which Diodore is commended, whom they say was blamed by Cyril together with Theodore and in the same cause, as teaching what Nestorius taught: so that, since Theodore could not justly be condemned without his teacher, with whom he shares a common cause, once we have proved that Diodore is not to be condemned, it may become all the more evident to everyone that Theodore was unjustly condemned solely to prejudice the synod of Chalcedon. Blessed Athanasius, then, writes thus to the said holy Diodore: "To my lord son and most beloved fellow priest, Diodore, bishop of Tarsus, Athanasius [sends] greeting in the Lord. Thanks to my Lord, who everywhere establishes his teaching, and especially through his own sons, such as the facts themselves show you to be.
passages.notes: 'Gratias Domino meo' may mean 'thanks to my Lord' (God); the letter's attribution to Athanasius is the author's claim.

passages.original: Qui tamen sanctum Diodorum nec in suspicionem hæresis venisse retulit: de quo sit ait: < Diodorus Tarsensis episcopus, dum Antiochiæ esset presbyter, magis cUrrit. Exstant ejus in Apostolo commentaria, et multa alia, ad Eusebii magis characterem pertinentia : cujus cum sensum secutus sit, eloquentiam imitari non potuit propter ignorantiam sæcularium litterarum. > Consonat autem bic sermo beati Hieronymi, quo refert eloquentia minorem Diodorum fuisse, verbis quæ memoravimus beati Basilii, quibus eidem Diodore scribens de libro quem ei miserat, dixit : Quia variatur sententiis, et facile in eo discernuntur econtrario oppositiones, et ad eas responsiones, et est oratione simplex , et sine ullo sermonis cothurno : quod convenire mibi visum est Christiani stylo, non ad ostentationem, sed ad utilitatem hominum scribentis.
passages.english: Yet he reported that Saint Diodorus had not even come under suspicion of heresy; of him he speaks thus: "Diodorus, bishop of Tarsus, while he was a presbyter at Antioch, was more renowned. There are extant his commentaries on the Apostle, and many other [works], belonging rather to the character of Eusebius; though he followed his sense, he could not imitate his eloquence because of his ignorance of secular letters." This statement of blessed Jerome, in which he reports that Diodorus was lesser in eloquence, agrees with the words of blessed Basil which we have mentioned, in which, writing to the same Diodorus about a book he had sent him, he said: "Because it is varied in its thoughts, and in it the objections from the opposing side and the replies to them are easily distinguished, and it is simple in style and without any buskin of speech; which seemed to me to suit the style of a Christian writing not for display but for the benefit of people."
passages.notes: "magis cUrrit" is evidently corrupt; Jerome's text reads "magis claruit" ("was more renowned"), translated accordingly. "sit ait" read as "sic ait".

passages.original: Dehinc etiam intelligimus quod sancta synodus prudenter inteNtionem Eutychis atque Ibae dijudicaus, sicut illum sacrilegum jusle damnavit, ejusque dogmat quamvis beatum Cyrillum laudaret, pronuntiavit hæreticum, quia fidem ipsius Cyrilli, quod magis attendendum fuerat, improbal: ita juste reverentissimum Ibam absolvit, ejusque epistolam, quamvis beatum Cyrillum vituperaret, pronuntiavit orthadoxam, quia fidem ipsius Cyrilli, quod magis atten- dendum fuerat, approbat. Vide quid ille præclarus episcopus inanis gloriæ studiosissimus contemptor 5, ct amator sincerissimus veritatis, 6 Augustinus dicat: < In cxordio librorum meorum opinaturus me sensisse quod non sensi: quorum errorem mihi tribui non debere quis nesciat, si velut me sequentes neque apprehendentes, deviaverint in aliquam falsitatem, dum per quædam densa et opaca cogor viam carpere? quandoquidem nec ipsis sanctis divinorum librorum auctoritatibus ullo modo quisquam recte tribuerit tam mullus et varios errores hæreticorum: cum omnes ex eisdem Scriptucis falsas atque fallaces opiniones suas conentur defendere.
passages.english: From this we also understand that the holy synod, wisely judging the intention of Eutyches and of Ibas, just as it justly condemned the former as sacrilegious and pronounced his teaching heretical, although he praised blessed Cyril, because he rejects the faith of Cyril himself, which was what ought more to be attended to; so it justly absolved the most reverend Ibas and pronounced his letter orthodox, although it censured blessed Cyril, because it approves the faith of Cyril himself, which was what ought more to be attended to. See what that illustrious bishop Augustine, a most earnest despiser of vain glory and a most sincere lover of truth, says: "At the beginning of my books [some will be] about to suppose that I held what I did not hold; who does not know that their error ought not to be attributed to me, if, as though following me and not grasping [me], they have strayed into some falsehood, while I am compelled to pick my way through certain dense and dark places? Since no one could in any way rightly attribute even to the holy authorities of the divine books themselves the so many and various errors of the heretics, when all of them try to defend their false and deceitful opinions from those same Scriptures."
passages.notes: "opinaturus me sensisse" is grammatically awkward (Augustine's text likely has "opinaturos" or similar); rendered by sense.

passages.original: Hæc sane orien- talium Patrum verba, quibus de Theodoro dixerunt: « Proponebat enim eum totus in commune Oricns inter eos qui ante nos fuerunt, sicut virtutem multam doctrinæ habentem adversus bxreses : » convenire serenitas tua cognoscit epistolæ beati Gregorii Nazianzeni, per quam eidem Thcodoro scribens ait : « Si quidem aliud caput haberet provincia, ad illud oporteret clamare et contestari; tua vero reverentia superposita, ad te attendere necesse est. » Et iterum : « Haec comprimere non est nostræ aetatis et infirmitatis, sed tuæ prudentiæ atque virtutis : quoniam tibi cum aliis facultatem donavit Omnipotens ad eommunem defensionem Ecclesiae.
passages.english: Your Serenity recognises that these words of the Eastern Fathers, in which they said of Theodore, "For the whole East commonly put him forward among those who were before us, as having great power of doctrine against heresies," agree with the letter of blessed Gregory Nazianzen, in which, writing to the same Theodore, he says: "If indeed the province had another head, it would be necessary to cry out and appeal to that; but since your Reverence is set over [it], it is necessary to look to you." And again: "To suppress these things is not a matter for our age and weakness, but for your prudence and virtue, since the Almighty has granted you, together with others, the ability for the common defence of the Church."

passages.original: sed la u- datorcs quidem horum illi in omni vita fuerunt, accusare autem cos nullus alicubi praesumpsit evidenter. » Apparet etiam ex his quae nunc protulimus, condiscipulum fuisse magni Joannis divulgatissimum Thcodorum, cum quo, ut Domnus attestatur, a sancto quoque Diodoro , sicut a .'laviano Antiochensi, piis dogmatibus enutritus est. Hoc etiam simul est proditum , quod odium contra Theodorum Eutychiani I ab ipso Eutyche patre suo contraxerint, qui divinitatem Uuigenili et humanitatem, unam naiuram vorabat, commixtionem et confusionem asscrens factam, cl salutarem passionem ipsi incontaminabili deitati adnectens.
passages.english: "but they were praisers of these men throughout their whole life, and no one anywhere dared openly to accuse them." It is apparent also from what we have now brought forward that the most celebrated Theodore was a fellow pupil of the great John, with whom, as Domnus attests, he was nourished in pious doctrines by Saint Diodorus as well as by Flavian of Antioch. At the same time this too is disclosed: that the Eutychians contracted their hatred against Theodore from Eutyches himself, their father, who called the divinity of the Only-begotten and the humanity one nature, asserting that a mixture and confusion had taken place, and attaching the saving passion to the undefilable deity itself.

passages.original: Nunquam enim, sicut didicimus, tantos ac tales simul habuit ductores Ecclesia, quantos et quales Diodori Theodorique temporibus. Ut enim propter linguæ diversitatem scientissimos viros Ecclesiæ occidentalis omittam, quanquam multi ex illis etiam in Graeco cruditi essent eloquio, ut Diodori atque Theodori scripta legentes. intentionem eorum cognoscere potuissent ; ut præteream et illos Græciæ doctissimos qui episcopi non fuerunt, cum eis Athanasius interea, Petrus, Timotheus ac Theophilus Alexandrini in verbi prædicatione degcrunt;
passages.english: For never, as we have learned, did the Church have at once so many and such great leaders as in the times of Diodorus and Theodore. For, to leave aside the most learned men of the Western Church because of the difference of language, although many of them were also learned in the Greek tongue, so that, reading the writings of Diodorus and Theodore, they could have known their intention; to pass over also those most learned men of Greece who were not bishops: alongside them in the meantime Athanasius, Peter, Timothy and Theophilus of Alexandria spent their lives in preaching the word;

passages.original: Quæ fuerat Joannis ac Procli Constantinopohtanorum, Gregorii Nazianzeni, Joannis ac Domni Antiochenorum et orientalis concilii fides, nec non Ecclesiæ a qua non est expulsus Theodorus, catietn fuerat et Cyrilli. De Theodoro tantum, sicut et du Diodoro, cui simul Athanasius :Itque 5 Constantinopolitana synodus attestatur, in solo Cyrillo dicitur inveniri diversa sententia; et quod est indicium certissimæ veritatis, in ipsa dissensione consensus unius ejusdemque fidei comprobatur.
passages.english: The faith which was that of John and Proclus of Constantinople, of Gregory Nazianzen, of John and Domnus of Antioch and of the Eastern council, and also of the Church from which Theodore was not expelled, was the same as that of Cyril too. Concerning Theodore alone, as also concerning Diodorus, to whom Athanasius and the synod of Constantinople together bear witness, a differing opinion is said to be found in Cyril alone; and, what is a sign of the most certain truth, in the very disagreement agreement in one and the same faith is proven.

passages.original: Si autem secundum humanitatem non est natura Filius Dei, necessario sequitur ut aut meritis, aut gratia sit Filius Dei 3, qui, ex quo esse coepit, non fuit aliud quam Filius Dei. Restat ergo ut secundat. humanitatem gratia sit Filius Dei. Ob hoc quoque beatus Augustinus, præcipuus catholicæ fidei prædicator, scr bens ad Prosperum et Hilarium de præ- destinatione sanctorum , et docens quod gratia Dei non secundum nostra merita detur, inter alia dicit (Lib. i, cap, 15): « Est etiam praeclarissimum lumen prædesticationis et gratiæ ipse Salvator, ipse mediator De! et hominum, homo Christus Jcsus : qui ut hoc esset, quibus tandem suis, vel operum, vel fidei praecedentibus meritis natura humana quæ in illo est comparavit ?
passages.english: But if according to the humanity the Son of God is not by nature, it necessarily follows that he is Son of God either by merits or by grace, he who, from the moment he began to exist, was nothing other than Son of God. It remains, therefore, that according to the humanity he is Son of God by grace. For this reason too blessed Augustine, the foremost preacher of the catholic faith, writing to Prosper and Hilary on the predestination of the saints, and teaching that the grace of God is not given according to our merits, says among other things (Book 1, ch. 15): "The most brilliant light of predestination and grace is the Saviour himself, the mediator himself between God and men, the man Christ Jesus: by what preceding merits of his own, whether of works or of faith, did the human nature that is in him acquire that it should be this?

passages.original: praesertim cum potuerit idem venerabilis ibas idcirco Theod rum ejusque laudare doctrinam, quoniam ea qu;e in libris ejus reprehensibilia judicabat, vel ab baereticis immissa, vel ab ipso Theodoro reprehensa, sicut docuimus, sive correcta esse credebat : et non ex eo quod scribendi capiens initium, aliqnid aliquando reprehensibile scripsit, aut ex lapsu sermon s incurrit, ejus doctrina judicanda fuerat; sed eo potius quod si quid in ea culpabile videbatur, ipse regrehendit atque correxit. Nam si ncmo sapiens Eccle- siam credit haereticam, quia doctrinam beati Cypriani Carthaginiensis episcopi et martyris laudat, cum ille non solum privatim, ut ei visum est, verum etiam congregato concilio, definierit ut omnis hæreticus ad Ecclesiam rediens baptizetur, et propter hoc culpatus ab Stephano antistite Romano restiterit, suamque sententiam scribens (Cyprian.
passages.english: especially since the same venerable Ibas could have praised Theodore and his teaching for this reason, that he believed the things he judged reprehensible in his books either to have been inserted by heretics, or, as we have shown, to have been censured or corrected by Theodore himself; and his teaching ought not to have been judged by the fact that, when beginning to write, he at some time wrote something reprehensible or fell into it through a slip of speech, but rather by this, that if anything in it seemed blameworthy, he himself censured and corrected it. For if no wise man believes the Church heretical because it praises the teaching of blessed Cyprian, bishop of Carthage and martyr, although he not only privately, as seemed good to him, but also in an assembled council, decreed that every heretic returning to the Church should be baptised, and when blamed for this by Stephen, bishop of Rome, resisted, and writing his opinion (Cyprian,
passages.notes: The sentence continues into the following passage.

passages.original: Athanasius, germanum specimen et probabile catholicæ doctrinae atque virtutis exemplum, ea constanter excepit, et quamvis nostris auribus dura et ad excusandum difficilia 1, defendere non reiugit, et prius eorum auctorein Dionysium per hoc voluit esse purgatum, atque ab Arianorum crimine alienum , quod ipse non sicut Arius, cum viveret, de impletate fuerit accusatus, aut de episcopatu dejectus; neque velut haeresim defendens, de Ecclesia sicut ille discesserit, sed in ejus permanse- rit unitate : deinde melius hæc ipsa interpretari conatus est.
passages.english: Athanasius, a genuine model and approved example of catholic doctrine and virtue, steadily took up these [statements], and although they were harsh to our ears and hard to excuse, he did not shrink from defending them. First he sought to show that their author Dionysius was cleared by this, and free of the charge of the Arians: that he, unlike Arius, had not been accused of impiety while he lived, nor deposed from the episcopate; nor had he left the Church as that man did, as one defending a heresy, but had remained in its unity. Then he tried to interpret these very [statements] in a better sense.
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: 'reiugit' read as 'refugit', 'auctorein' as 'auctorem', 'impletate' as 'impietate'. The '1' after 'difficilia' is a footnote mark and has been omitted.

passages.original: Et iterum (Cap. 27) : « Confirmantes Christianismi intellectum, dicimus quoniam si quis Christum Deum Filium Dei ante sæcula subsistentem et ministrantem Patri ad omnium perfectionem non dicat, sed ex quo de Maria natus est, ei eo et Christum et Filium nomlnatum esse, et initium accepisse ut sit Deus, dicat, anatbema sit. » Quae omnia memoratum Sirmiense concilium * sanctus Hilarius necessarie contra Photinum et 4 Orientales asserit decrevisse. Quorum sufficientem excusationem faciens, quomodo sint accipienda demonstrai. Hæc ergo Atbanasio, haec Basilio, hæc Hilario et omnibus viris sanctis sollicitudo fuit, ne culpatis velut haereticis eis qui in Ecclesiæ pace atque honore defuncti sunt, ipsa quae illos magno honore dignata est Ecclesia culparetur.
passages.english: And again (ch. 27): "Confirming the understanding of Christianity, we say that if anyone does not say that Christ, God, the Son of God, subsisted before the ages and ministered to the Father for the completion of all things, but says that from the time he was born of Mary, from then he was named both Christ and Son, and received a beginning so as to be God, let him be anathema." All of which Saint Hilary asserts that the said council of Sirmium decreed of necessity against Photinus and the Easterners. Making a sufficient excuse for them, he shows how they are to be understood. This, then, was the concern of Athanasius, this of Basil, this of Hilary and of all holy men: that by blaming as heretics those who died in the peace and honour of the Church, the Church itself, which deemed them worthy of great honour, should not be blamed.

passages.original: Multa vero superioribus similia ex dictis ejusdem beati Eustacliii proferre possemus, quæ possent in uno * tractari volumine ; sed ista legenti sufficiant, quoniam volumus ad aliorum scriptu transire, de quibus æque uon omnia quæ his similia dixerunt sed aliqua tantummodo proferimus. Quid ergo etiam. sanctus Athanasius dicat in epistola ad Antiochenos a dehcmus inspicere : « Ex veteribus enim eruditus 1 et legis doctor existens, Proverbia Salomonis legens et duas personas de Domino inveniens, unam quidem circa hominem quem ei Maria pro nobis futurus erat assumere, alteram autem circa Verbum quod ante omnia sæcula æterne ex Patre natum est;
passages.english: We could bring forward many things similar to the above from the sayings of the same blessed Eustathius, which could fill a single volume; but let these suffice the reader, since we wish to pass on to the writings of others, from whom likewise we bring forward not everything they said similar to these but only some things. Let us therefore also examine what Saint Athanasius says in the letter to the Antiochenes: "For being instructed from the ancients and a teacher of the law, reading the Proverbs of Solomon and finding two persons concerning the Lord, one concerning the man whom Mary was to assume for him on our behalf, the other concerning the Word who was born eternally from the Father before all ages;
passages.notes: The attribution to Athanasius is as the text gives it. "quem ei Maria ... assumere" is syntactically odd; rendered by sense.

passages.original: » Ergone huic tutum, sicut credidit, non esset hoc placitum pium coram Domino Deo nostro cum omnibus qui sua legerent initum, etiamsi non admonitus in aliquo permansisset crrore? quis nisi crudelis aut dicat aut credat? Tales igitur æstimemus et alios doctores Ecclesiae, qualem se nobis Augustinus ostendit? et nullum dicemus haereticum in Ecclesiae pace atque honore defuncfum. Quid enim me lædit, si de omnibus taliter sentiam, vel si non omnes fuerint tales? Hic forsitan aliquis dicat : Sed de Augustino recte sic audis 2 , cujus animum professio sua declarat: de aliis autem qua ratione sic credas?
passages.english: "Would this pious agreement, then, entered into before the Lord our God with all who would read his writings, not have been safe for him, as he believed, even if, not having been admonished, he had remained in some error? Who but a cruel man would either say or believe [that]? Shall we therefore consider the other doctors of the Church to be such as Augustine has shown himself to us? And we shall say that no one who died in the peace and honour of the Church was a heretic. For what harm does it do me if I think this way about all of them, even if not all were such? Here perhaps someone may say: 'But you rightly think so of Augustine, whose mind his own declaration makes plain; but on what ground do you believe so of the others?'
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected silently: 'crrore' (errore), 'defuncfum' (defunctum). 'audis' is probably a misreading of 'credis' or 'sentis' ('think'); the footnote mark '2' omitted. The first sentence of the second paragraph may be meant as a statement rather than a question despite the edition's punctuation ('Let us therefore consider...').

passages.original: » Aliter itaque, sicut iste vir prudentissimus docet, canonicas litteras legimus, in quibus necesse est etiam quod non credimus, cum invenerimu, incunctanter credere; aliter autem, vel ipsius Augustini, vel talium cælerorum; in quihus quod habemus incertum, nisi certum intellexerimus, non firme ret nere debemus. Qui etiam Hieronymo scribens dicit (Epist. 19) : « Ego enim fateor charitati tuæ, solis eis Scriptura- rum libris quae jam canonicæ appellantur didici hunc timorem bonoremque deferre, ut nullum eorum auctorem scribendo errasse aliquid firmissime credam ; ac si aliquid in eis offendero litteris quod videatur contrarium veritati, nihil aliud quam vel mendosum rsse codicem , vel interpretem non assecutum esse quod dictum est, vel me minime intellexisse non ambigam.
passages.english: "So, as this most prudent man teaches, we read the canonical writings in one way, in which, when we have found even what we do not [yet] believe, we must believe it without hesitation; but in another way [the writings] either of Augustine himself or of others like him, in which we ought not to hold firmly what we regard as uncertain unless we have understood it to be certain. He also, writing to Jerome, says (Epist. 19): 'For I confess to your charity that I have learned to pay this reverence and honour only to those books of the Scriptures which are now called canonical, so that I most firmly believe that none of their authors erred in anything in writing; and if I come upon anything in those writings that seems contrary to the truth, I shall not doubt that either the manuscript is faulty, or the translator has not grasped what was said, or I have failed to understand it.
